frame.name: Dock 26 · alo working in selected window

text.name: v0.01 · Left, right and top · Existing canvas, consistent controls
Top controls are system overlays, not a reserved desktop band. Hidden in full screen; edge reveal or keyboard focus restores them. Return restores the same Place, window geometry and canvas camera.
Top Dock: first row y16–92. Window controls: second row y104–164. Shelf begins below y180. Surfaces never overlap or displace app content. Empty overlay space must not intercept app clicks.

Side Dock + shelf on the same edge: shelf owns y84–180 of the edge; Dock owns y192–960. Dock occupies the outer lane (x24–92 left, x1348–1416 right). The expanded shelf opens inward at x116 or x1072. The 12px gap is a hover-safe travel corridor, not a click blocker.

Reveal is latched while pointer is in the assigned strip, actual surface or its travel corridor; also while keyboard focus, a child menu or drag belongs to it. No hide delay. Only active surface regions intercept clicks; hover-only regions do not.

Dock size is content-driven, with 24 logical px margins after reserved regions. Icons may reduce from 32 to 28; targets remain 44×44. At the limit, overflow keeps all applications reachable. Never shrink text or rotate the composer.

Keyboard: Tab moves through visible controls; arrow keys follow Dock orientation; Home / End select first / last app; Enter focuses; Escape closes a menu first. Use the existing system-control shortcut to reveal and focus; do not invent a new shortcut mapping.

Accessibility: tooltip and spoken name on each icon; return focus to the invoker; selected/open indicators do not rely on colour. Reduced transparency uses the same opaque surface token. RTL changes reading order/default edge, never overrides an explicit edge preference.

Prototype: each orientation has a start. More opens overflow, search opens the side composer; Return goes back to canvas. The full-screen reveal uses a continuous hover region. These are interaction states; native dragging, typed search, permissions and rendering still need Rust integration.
